In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah Al-Mujadila.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those of you who divorce [by zihar] their wives, [saying to them, "You are to me like the back of my mother"] — they are not their mothers.﴾ up to His saying: ﴿then feeding sixty needy persons﴾.

We have already presented the discussion of this verse in detail in Surah Al-Ahzab, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 4]. There we explained the statements of the scholars and their evidences, and their debate, concerning the rulings of zihar, the rulings on the expiation (kaffarah) by freeing a slave, by fasting, and by feeding, and the readings (wujuh al-qira'ah) of the verse.

[p-410]

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

Surah al-Mujadila

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who divorce by zihar (pronouncing their wives unlawful like their mothers' backs) from among their wives, then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before they touch one another.﴾

It is not hidden that His ordering of the expiation by manumission upon the zihar and the return together implies that the expiation is not obligatory except by the zihar and the return together.

And His saying: ﴿before they touch one another﴾ is explicit that the expiation must be prior to the return to touching (al-masis).

Know first that what Ibn Hazm preferred from the view of Dawud, and what Ibn Abd al-Barr related from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, al-Farra', and a group of the people of kalam (theology), and what Shu'ba held, namely that the meaning of ﴿then go back on what they said﴾ is their returning to the wording of zihar, so that they repeat it a second time, is a false view. The evidence is that the Prophet ﷺ did not ask the woman concerning whom the verse of zihar was revealed whether her husband had repeated the formula of zihar or not, and leaving out such questioning (tark al-istifsal) takes the place of generality in statements, as has been mentioned many times before.

The correct position is that the expiation and the prohibition of intercourse before it do not require the repetition of the formula of zihar. What some have also alleged, that the statement contains inversion and transposition, its intended sense being: ﴿Those who divorce by zihar from among their wives, then the freeing of a slave before they touch one another, then they go back on what they said, being free of sin through the expiation﴾, is also not valid, because it is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) that the order must be kept as it is unless there is evidence otherwise. To this the author of Maraqi al-Su'ud alludes in his words:

"Likewise the order stands to make obligatory the acting upon what is most probable among what is possible."

We shall mention, if Allah wills, the answer to this difficulty according to the schools of the four Imams, may Allah be pleased with them all, and so we say, and in Allah we seek help:

Regarding the meaning of al-awd (return) according to Malik, there are two statements. The Mudawwana has been interpreted as supporting each of them, and both are preferred.

[p-411]

The first: it is resolve (al-'azm) upon intercourse only.

The second: it is resolve upon intercourse together with keeping the wife (al-imsak).

On both statements there is no difficulty in the verse, because the meaning then is: ﴿Those who divorce by zihar from among their wives, then they resolve upon intercourse, or upon it together with keeping, then the freeing of a slave before they touch one another﴾. So there is no contradiction between resolve upon intercourse, or upon it with keeping, and manumission before touching.

The most that this view entails is the omission of the verb "intend" (hadhf al-irada), which occurs in the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿When you stand up for the prayer﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 6], meaning "when you intend to stand for it."

And His saying: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an﴾ [al-Nahl: 98], meaning "when you intend to recite it, then seek refuge in Allah," the verse [al-Nahl: 98].

According to al-Shafi'i, the meaning of al-awd is that he keeps her after the zihar for a period of time in which he could divorce her, but he does not divorce her. On this view too there is no difficulty in the verse, because his keeping her for the stated period does not contradict the expiation before touching, as is clear.

According to Ahmad, the meaning of al-awd is that he returns to intercourse or resolves upon it. As for resolve, we have already explained that there is no difficulty in the verse on that view.

As for the view that it means intercourse itself, the answer is that if he committed zihar and had intercourse before the expiation, it becomes obligatory for him to refrain from touching her once more until he has made expiation. From this it does not follow that the first intercourse before the expiation is permissible, because the verse on this view only explains the ruling for the case where intercourse occurred before the expiation, namely that expiation becomes obligatory before another touching.

As for proceeding to the first touching, its prohibition is known from the generality of His saying: ﴿before they touch one another﴾.

According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, the meaning of al-awd is resolve upon sexual intercourse (al-wat'), and on this view there is no difficulty, as has been mentioned.

As for what Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, related in his tafsir from Malik, that he reported from him that al-awd is intercourse, this is contrary to the known position of his school.

[p-412]

Likewise what he related from Abu Hanifa, that al-awd is a return to zihar after its prohibition and the abolition of what the matter was in the Jahiliyya, is contrary to what is established in the furu' (derivative rulings) of the Hanafi school, namely that it is resolve upon intercourse, as we mentioned. Most of what has been said about the meaning of al-awd goes back to the statements of the Imams that we have mentioned, may Allah have mercy on them.

Some scholars said: the intended meaning of al-awd is a return to enjoyment (al-istimta') without intercourse, and the intended meaning of al-masis in His saying ﴿before they touch one another﴾ is specifically intercourse.

On this view there is no difficulty, but it is not hidden that this view is not evident. The correct position is that enjoyment, whether by intercourse or otherwise, is not permitted before the expiation, because of the generality of His saying: ﴿before they touch one another﴾.

Some permitted enjoyment other than intercourse, saying: the intended meaning of al-masis in His saying ﴿before they touch one another﴾ is intercourse itself, not its preliminaries.

Among those who said this are al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Thawri.

It is related from al-Shafi'i as one of his two statements. Some scholars said: the lam in His saying "li-ma qalu" (for what they said) has the meaning of fi (in), so that the meaning is "they return in what they said," meaning "they retract from it," as in the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "The one who gives a gift and then takes it back is like a dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit," the hadith. It was also said: the lam has the meaning of 'an (from), meaning "they go back from what they said," that is, they retract it, and this is close to what came before.

The one who wrote this, may Allah pardon him, says: What appears, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that al-awd has a beginning and an end. Its beginning is resolve upon intercourse, and its end is intercourse in actuality. Whoever resolves upon intercourse has returned in intention, so the expiation becomes obligatory for him because intercourse has been made permissible. Whoever has intercourse in actuality, the obligation becomes certain for him, and he has opposed (the ruling) by proceeding to intercourse before the expiation. What indicates this is that when the Prophet ﷺ said: "When two Muslims meet with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we understand the killer, but what about the killed?" He said: "He was eager to kill his companion." So he clarified that resolve to commit an act is an action for which a person is held accountable.

If it is said: the apparent meaning of the verse, which comes first to the mind from it, agrees with the view of the Zahiriyya which we have already shown to be invalid, because the apparent meaning which comes first from His saying "li-ma qalu" is the formula of zihar, so that al-awd to it would be repeating it a second time.

The answer is that the meaning of "li-ma qalu" is that it is forbidden for them, namely intercourse. This is indicated by the existence of a parallel to it in the Qur'an, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will inherit what he says﴾ [Maryam: 80], meaning what he claims he will be given of wealth and children, in His saying: ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾ [Maryam: 77]. And what we mentioned, that whoever has intercourse before the expiation becomes obliged to refrain from touching her once more until he has made expiation, is the correct position, in contrast to the view of those who said: the expiation falls away by intercourse before touching.

As was related from al-Zuhri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Abu Yusuf. And to those who said: two expiations become obligatory by it.

As was related from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. And to those who said: three expiations become obligatory by it, as Sa'id ibn Mansur related from al-Hasan and Ibrahim. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you not see that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth? There is no private conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

We have already presented the discussion of this in the end of Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [an-Nahl: 128]. There we mentioned the meaning of the special companionship (al-ma'iyyah al-khassah) and the general companionship (al-ma'iyyah al-'ammah), and the Qur'anic verses that indicate each one of them.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret consultation, then they return to that which they were forbidden, and they consult together in sin and transgression?﴾

We have already presented the discussion of this verse, along with an explanation of the distinction between secret consultation for good and secret consultation for sin and transgression, in Surat an-Nisa' in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret consultation, except for one who orders charity, or what is good, or reconciliation between people﴾ [an-Nisa': 114].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 12:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, present before your private consultation a charity.﴾

This verse indicates the requirement of offering charity before private consultation (munajah).

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Are you apprehensive about presenting before your private consultation charities? So when you do not do so and Allah has forgiven you...﴾ — the verse [al-Mujadila: 13] — indicates the opposite of that.

The answer is evident, namely that the latter abrogates the former (naskh), and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 14:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry? They are neither of you nor of them﴾.

Some of the scholars (ahl al-'ilm) said: The meaning of ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies﴾ is: Has your knowledge not reached to those who have taken as allies?

We have already presented the refutation of the one who said that the expression "alam tara" (have you not considered) is not transitive except with the preposition "ila" (to), which is the particle of genitive (harf al-jarr), and that it is not transitive by itself to the object. We clarified that although this is what occurs in the Qur'an in all its places, its transitivity to the object by itself is sound.

Among the evidence for this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"Have you not seen me, whenever I came to Tariq, found in her a fragrance, even though she was not perfumed?"

The intended meaning is Allah's denunciation of the hypocrites for their allying with the people with whom Allah is angry, namely the Jews and the disbelievers. This denunciation indicates the severity of the prohibition of that alliance. Allah has explicitly forbidden it in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 13].

What this noble verse contains, namely that the hypocrites are neither of the believers nor of the people they have allied with, who are those with whom Allah is angry from among the Jews, has been made clear in another place, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites try to deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them... wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾ [an-Nisa': 142-143].

The Exalted said in this noble verse: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they have barred others from the way of Allah; for them there is a humiliating punishment.﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted and Majestic mentions that the hypocrites have taken their oaths as a shield. Al-aymān (oaths) is the plural of yamīn, which means an oath. Al-junnah is the shield with which a fighter protects himself from the impact of weapons. The meaning is that they made their false oaths, by which they swore to the Muslims that they were with them and sincere inwardly, into a shield for themselves, by which they guard against the harm that would befall them if they openly declared their disbelief.

The Exalted's words ﴿so they have barred others from the way of Allah﴾ apparently derive from ṣadda, which is transitive (mutaʿaddiyah, taking a direct object), and its object is omitted. That is, they barred others from the way of Allah, namely those who obeyed them. Their own turning away is already indicated by His words ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾. Interpreting the phrase as establishing a new meaning (taʾsīs) is preferable to interpreting it as emphasis (taʾkīd), as we have explained many times.

These two matters that this noble verse contains, namely that the hypocrites swear false oaths so that these become a shield for them, and that they bar others from the way of Allah, are both explained in other verses of the Book of Allah. As for their false oaths, Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, has clarified them in many verses:

• such as the Exalted's words in this surah: ﴿They swear falsely by Allah while they know﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 14],

• and His words: ﴿They swear to you by Allah in order to please you, while Allah and His Messenger have more right to be pleased, if they are believers﴾,

• and His words: ﴿They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone; indeed, they are defilement, and their refuge is Hell﴾ [al-Tawbah: 95], to the end of the verse, (p-٥٥٤)

• and His words: ﴿They will swear by Allah, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you." They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars﴾ [al-Tawbah: 42],

• and His words: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they have barred others from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 2].

As for their barring of those who obeyed them from the way of Allah, Allah has clarified this in verses of His Book:

• such as His words: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder others, and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18],

• and His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers, when they traveled through the land or were raiders, "Had they remained with us, they would not have died or been killed"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 156],

• and His words: ﴿Those who said of their brothers while they sat [at home], "Had they obeyed us, they would not have been killed"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 168],

• and His words: ﴿Indeed, among you is one who will surely lag behind﴾ [al-Nisa': 72].

The Exalted's words in this noble verse, ﴿for them there is a humiliating punishment﴾, mean: because of their hypocrisy, as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [al-Nisa': 145], to the end of the verse.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself﴾, through to His saying: ﴿a better return than it﴾ [al-Kahf: 35-36].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Devil has overcome them, so he has made them forget the remembrance of Allah.﴾

What this noble verse includes of attributing the causing of forgetting the remembrance of Allah to the Devil—He, the Exalted, mentioned it in other than this place, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if the Devil causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-An'am: 68], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So the Devil caused him to forget the remembrance of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf: 42]. And in its meaning is the saying of Musa's young companion: ﴿And none caused me to forget it except the Devil, that I should mention it﴾ [al-Kahf: 63].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 20:

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated.﴾

In this noble verse, He - Majestic and Exalted - mentions that those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are included among the most humiliated; there is no one more humiliated than them. His saying ﴿those who oppose (yuhadduna) Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: they show enmity, they side against them, and they oppose them (yushaqqqunahu). Its root meaning is the violation of the limits (hudud, "bounds") of Allah which He has set.

His saying ﴿among the most humiliated (al-adhallin)﴾ means: those who are the greatest of people in humiliation. Adhdhull (humiliation) is abasement, disgrace, and lowliness.

What this noble verse includes, namely that those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are the most humiliated of Allah's creation, Allah - Majestic and Exalted - has explained in other places, by mentioning the kinds of punishment for them that lead to humiliation, disgrace, and degradation,

such as the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever? That is the great disgrace.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 63],

and the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be humiliated (kubitu), as those before them were humiliated.﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 5],

and the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if not that Allah had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.﴾ ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes Allah - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.﴾ [Al-Hashr: 3-4],

and the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So strike [them] above the necks and strike from them every fingertip.﴾ ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.﴾ ﴿That, so taste it; and indeed, for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 12-14],

and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 21:

The words of the Most High: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed God is Strong, Mighty.﴾

This noble verse indicates that the messengers of God prevail over everyone who opposes them. Victory (al-ghalabah) is of two kinds: victory by proof and clear explanation, which is established for all the messengers; and victory by the sword and the spear, which is established only for those among them who were commanded to fight, and not for those who were not commanded to do so.

This noble verse, and similar verses like the words of the Most High: ﴿And certainly Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed they would be the ones given victory. And indeed Our soldiers will be the victors﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173], indicate that no prophet has ever been killed in jihad, because the one who is killed is not a victor, since being killed is a category opposed to victory. This is what He explained in His words: ﴿And whoever fights in the way of God and is killed or achieves victory﴾ [al-Nisa': 74], and the Most High said: ﴿Indeed We will surely help Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. He also categorically negated that the one who is helped could be defeated, in His words: ﴿If God helps you, none can overcome you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 160].

From this you know that the messengers of whom the Qur'an says they were killed, such as the words of the Most High: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you grew arrogant, so you denied some and some you kill?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87], and His words: ﴿Say: "Messengers before me certainly came to you with clear proofs and with what you spoke of. Why, then, did you kill them?"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 183], were not killed in jihad. And the subject (na'ib al-fa'il) in the words of the Most High (p-556) ﴿And many prophets have fought, along with them, large groups of devoted men [rabbiyyun]﴾ [Al 'Imran: 146], according to the reading "qutila" in the passive voice, is rabbiyyun, not the pronoun of the prophet.

We have clarified this to the utmost degree with Qur'anic verses in the surah of Al 'Imran, in discussing the words of the Most High: ﴿And many prophets have fought, along with them, large groups of devoted men﴾ [Al 'Imran: 146], and we mentioned part of it in al-Saffat, in discussing the words of the Most High: ﴿And certainly Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers﴾ [al-Saffat: 171].
